name: Kokkola
title: Kokkola Bulk Carrier UTM: Hull and Hold Thickness Gauging
description: Thickness measurement in Kokkola for bulk carriers, chemical tankers and container feeders: hold, tank top, ballast tank and deck gauging at the Deep Port.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement at Kokkola, Finland's Main Bulk Port
intro: Kokkola, on the Finnish coast of the Gulf of Bothnia, is the country's largest bulk port. Its Deep Port takes bulk carriers and tankers serving the Kokkola Industrial Park and the mines and mills inland, while Silverstone Port handles containers and wind turbine components. Long bulk discharges, abrasive and corrosive cargoes and a hard ice season make hold and tank gauging a regular need here. We send technicians from India to the ship for each job, timed to her berth window.
keywords: chemical tanker gauging gulf of bothnia

highlights.h: Deep bulk berths in the Bay
highlights.p: The Deep Port's fairway was recently deepened for ships drawing up to fourteen metres. It brings bulk carriers larger than most ports on this coast can take, and with them ESP survey scopes and the hold wear that dense mineral cargoes cause.

Ore and metal concentrates, minerals and process chemicals for the Kokkola Industrial Park are hard on holds and cargo tanks. Abrasion from grabs and corrosion from damp residues thin tank tops, hopper plating and frames faster than a clean grain trade would.

highlights.h: Containers and wind components at Silverstone
highlights.p: Silverstone Port handles container feeders and project ships carrying wind turbine parts for inland wind farms. Feeders run tight rotations, so their gauging is planned in stages, while project calls give longer windows alongside for deck and tank work.

port.h: Kokkola's three harbours and their trades
p: Kokkola lies just north of the Kvarken, on the southern shores of the Bay of Bothnia, and its port is spread across three areas west of the town. The General Port is the oldest, with roots in the early nineteenth century, and today handles general cargo and light bulk, including an all-weather terminal where cargo can be worked under cover. Silverstone Port takes containers and project cargo, has a new container gantry crane and is being expanded for wind turbine components. The Deep Port is the largest of the three, built for dry and liquid bulk, with a long quay line and a fairway deepened in recent years. Each area brings different ships, and so a different gauging scope for the team to prepare.

The Deep Port is where most of the tonnage goes. It serves the Kokkola Industrial Park, a large concentration of chemical and metals industry where zinc and cobalt are refined and battery materials are made, and it also handles heavy raw materials for mines and mills across central and northern Finland. Ships discharge ore and metal concentrates, minerals and other dense cargoes, and load products and by-products, while chemical tankers use the liquid bulk berths. Bulk carriers range from small handysize ships to the larger types that only the deepened fairway admits. Discharging dense cargo by grab is unhurried work, and ships often spend several days alongside, which is time a gauging team can use without delaying the ship.

Winter shapes everything at Kokkola. The sea freezes every year, ships need an ice class that meets the Finnish winter traffic restrictions, and icebreakers lead traffic through the fairway in the hardest months. Many bulk carriers are built for open-water trades and carry a modest ice class or none, so trading into Kokkola in the deepest ice tends to fall to ships with higher classes, which then take the ice-belt wear that goes with it. The water level, as everywhere in the Baltic, rises and falls with wind and air pressure rather than tides, and the gradual land uplift on this coast keeps the port watching its depths. Open-hatch, dry-weather tasks suit the summer, but holds and tanks can be measured in any month.

facilities.h: Gauging at the Deep Port, Silverstone and the General Port
p: At the Deep Port the usual pattern is hold by hold. As each hold is emptied the team moves in to measure tank top, hopper and lower stool plating, frames and brackets, then the topside and double-bottom tanks the crew has opened, ventilated and certified for entry. Concentrate residues hide pitting and grooving, so reading points are cleaned locally, and hold frames at the lower brackets, where grab damage concentrates, get a closer reading pattern. Chemical tankers at the liquid berths are a different job: cargo tanks stay closed during operations, so the scope is deck, piping and ballast tanks, with cargo tank internals left for a gas-free period.

Container feeders and project ships at Silverstone Port are gauged alongside within their port stay, and the covered terminal at the General Port suits general cargo ships whose holds are worked in any weather, which helps when a job falls in a wet autumn. We do not plan full renewal-survey dockings in Kokkola; the ships trading here are usually docked by their owners at repair yards in southern Finland or elsewhere around the Baltic. Measuring a ship during a Kokkola discharge, weeks before her docking, gives the chosen yard a steel list it can plan around.

Deep Port liquid-bulk berths — chemical tankers; deck plating, cargo and ballast piping and ballast tanks inside the terminal's permit system
Silverstone Port — container feeders and project ships with wind turbine components; staged deck and tank gauging within the port stay

context.h: Inspection regime, ice classes and the industrial trade at Kokkola
p: Ships calling at Kokkola come under Paris MoU port state control, carried out in Finland by Traficom. Bulk carriers and chemical tankers count as higher-risk ship types in the regime's targeting, and age adds to a ship's risk score once she passes twelve years, so the older bulk tonnage on the Kokkola trade is inspected with some attention to hold condition. Because so much of the traffic is ESP bulk carriers, the renewal and intermediate surveys that fall due on these ships carry the full ESP gauging requirements, with transverse sections and close-up survey of selected frames, and a Kokkola discharge is a sensible moment to prepare that work.

The Finnish winter traffic restrictions are the other rule that governs Kokkola. They are set each season for every port, naming the lowest ice class and the minimum size of ship that will be given icebreaker assistance, and they tighten as the ice thickens. A bulk carrier fixed for a winter cargo must meet them on arrival, so charterers check the ice class and owners need confidence that the ice belt still carries the scantlings the class demands. Kokkola's industrial customers sit in the battery-materials and energy-transition supply chain, and their steady demand for concentrates and chemicals brings the same ships back again and again, which suits gauging spread over several visits.

jobs.h: What a gauging job at Kokkola usually involves
jobs.p: Most Kokkola work is bulk carrier gauging during discharge: survey preparation, owner's condition checks and the measurements that tell a superintendent how far hold steel has gone. Chemical tankers and container feeders add smaller scopes, and the project trade brings occasional work on heavy-lift ships. Because many bulk carriers return to Kokkola on regular contracts, owners can split a large renewal-survey scope across two or three calls rather than leaving everything for the dock, which shortens the docking and removes surprises from the steel list. Winter jobs are planned with a margin for icebreaker delays and for the longer ventilation that cold tanks need.
list: ESP intermediate-survey gauging on a bulk carrier discharging concentrates at the Deep Port, covering hold frames, tank top and selected ballast tanks
Hold and hopper plating measured on a handysize bulk carrier to assess grab damage and pitting before her next renewal survey
Deck, piping and ballast-tank gauging on a chemical tanker at the liquid berths, with cargo tank internals planned for a later gas-free period
Ice-belt and bow gauging on a bulk carrier fixed for winter trading, to confirm the scantlings behind her Finnish-Swedish ice class
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a container feeder during a Silverstone Port call, set out for the buyer before the sale closes

logistics: Kokkola-Pietarsaari Airport, a short drive from the town, is served through Helsinki, and Kokkola is also on the main rail line between Helsinki and Oulu, which gives the team a second route north if winter flights are disrupted. Our technicians travel from India on Schengen visas, so we fix the job date as soon as the ship's laycan or berth window is firm. The ship's agent requests ISPS passes for the Deep Port, Silverstone or the General Port, and the terminal's own safety induction is completed on arrival.

faqs.q: Can bulk carriers be gauged during discharge at the Deep Port?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the usual way. Each hold is measured once it is empty while the next is still being discharged, and ballast and topside tanks follow under the ship's entry permits. Concentrate dust and residue are cleaned off locally at each reading point. The aim is to finish within the discharge, so the gauging never adds port days; anything left over is listed for the next call.

faqs.q: Why do hold frames on the Kokkola trade wear so quickly?
faqs.a: Heavy concentrates and minerals are usually discharged by grab, and the lower part of hold frames, the brackets and the hopper plating take impacts that remove coating and dent the steel. Damp residues then corrode those bare areas between cargoes. We take a denser reading pattern at the lower frame ends and brackets and record pitting and grooving depths, because those are the details a surveyor will look at most closely.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a chemical tanker's cargo tanks in Kokkola?
faqs.a: Only when they are gas-free. During cargo operations at the liquid berths we measure deck plating, the outside of cargo and ballast piping, and ballast tanks the crew has certified safe. Cargo tank structure needs gas-free certification and often cleaning as well, so for a renewal-survey or condition scope we plan that part for a gas-free period or for the docking.

faqs.q: Will ice stop a winter gauging job in Kokkola?
faqs.a: It changes the logistics more than the work. Ships may wait for icebreaker assistance and arrive later than planned, and readings on the outer shell are limited when ice lies against the hull. Inside, tanks and holds are measured as normal once spaces are ventilated, using couplant that copes with sub-zero temperatures. We build waiting time into winter plans and keep in daily contact with the agent.

faqs.q: Can a large renewal-survey scope be split over several Kokkola calls?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Ships on regular contracts to the Kokkola Industrial Park return frequently, so holds, tanks and transverse sections can be measured over two or three discharges and compiled into one owner's record. The superintendent then uses that record to fix the steel list and the dock days before the docking, and the docking itself concentrates on the bottom, the shell and the renewal work.
